chapter_theme: ஞானம் - 3, headed 'this knowledge is for living without hesitating': no one knows where the life goes at death, and the sayings about joining the sky-Siva or fire joining fire are the talk of people who do not know the embryo. The run then gives its own account of scripture: the ancients, Vyasa among them at Siva's order, made up stories, epics and Puranas, six shastras, dharma and adharma, heaven, hell and rebirth, gurus and disciples, to hold the bewildered and for livelihood, and the reader is told to see this clearly.
structure_note: Six stanzas chaining by antadi (மாடே / மாடு; தயங்கி / [missing]; பாடினாரே / பாடினதோர்; தானே / கழிந்திடுவார் loosely). 2420 and 2421 are on death and the unknowing crowd; 2422 to 2425 are one connected argument about the making of the Puranas and the shastras. 2422 has seven lines and no antadi opening, so its first line is probably lost.

2420.reading: Look: when the life leaves, some say a ruined corpse lies there, some say the life has gone; who has known it? No one; some say it joins the sky-Siva, some say fire joins fire, a crowd of human beings who do not know the embryo; the lustful band together and go seeking the evil way, like cattle.
2420.nuance: The verse reports four sayings about death and rejects all of them with ஆரும் இல்லை, no one has known. கருவறியா, not knowing the embryo, makes the knowledge of conception (2409, 2411) the test of knowing death: the way out is the way in. மாடே, 'like cattle', carries into 2421 by antadi.

2421.reading: Even cattle have one way of going, but man does not know even that much; they say much about hell and heaven, and do not reckon good deed or bad; listen: the dancing goddesses do not think even of joining the kin of the rare Father; they think pointedly of women to ravish, and hesitate at falling into the ground-fire.
2421.nuance: The middle lines are hard: ஆடுகின்ற தேவதைகள் (the dancing deities) may be the gods of the Puranas, who in the next verses are shown as inventions, or the dancing-women; and தளமான தீயில் விழத் தயங்கினார் (hesitated to fall into the fire of the floor) may be the pyre or the fire of lust. The clear claim is that people talk of heaven and hell while reckoning neither deed nor consequence.

2422.reading: The knowledge praised at large is something else; see the knowledge made to bewilder: the ancients gathered and tied on stories, kavyas and Puranas, as though fire had entered the natural essence, and set them to music as 'the six shastras'; and Vyasa too, so that the field might yield, tied them on at Siva's order.
2422.nuance: The stanza has seven lines and lacks the antadi opening expected after தயங்கினாரே, so a line is probably lost, and இயலான ரசந்தனிலீப் புகுந்தாற் போலும் is obscure (perhaps 'like fire entering mercury', an alchemical figure for adulteration). The verse's own heading says this knowledge is 'for living without hesitating'. The charge that Vyasa made the Puranas at Siva's order is repeated in 2423, where the aim is a hidden play (கபடநாடகம்).

2423.reading: Showing the Puranas as proof in this way, they made stories like the Bharata in the world, so as not to let one think that the Maker is oneself; adding deceit as a hidden play, singing much disputation as if it were substance, with treachery, for all who joined the way as true, and pouring on ornament for the Saivas as devotion, they sang the shastras, they sang.
2423.nuance: The key charge is கர்த்தாவைத் தானென்று தோண வொட்டா, not letting one realise that the Maker is oneself: the Puranas are read as a device to keep God external. மேதஞ் சேர்த்து (adding மேதம், deceit or sacrifice) is uncertain. The verse does not spare the Saivas, whose devotion it calls ornament poured on. Whether 'they' are the ancients of 2422 or Vyasa alone is not fixed.

2424.reading: Listen to the way they sang it, the light called the Bharata and the Puranas: that a long-lived Ravana was born, that steadfast Dasaratha's hand conquered, that there was a long-lived king, a sage, one who had received full grace, a god, a dancing demon, a man; they sang it every day as enmity.
2424.nuance: The verse reduces the Ramayana and the Puranas to a cast list (demon, king, sage, god, man) and says their daily theme is enmity (பகையாய்). சோதி (light) for the Bharata-Purana is ironic or a received epithet. The claim is literary and moral, that the epics teach division, rather than that their events are false; 2425 extends it to the doctrines they carry.

2425.reading: The four Vedas and six shastras that bind people say they will perish by sin, and said it only so that it might cease, nothing else; they made two, adharma and dharma, said one escapes, said there is birth and 'I shall be born noble'; and the worldly who are clear say 'gurus' and 'disciples'; all this is for livelihood, see it clearly.
2425.nuance: The reading of அழிந்திடவே சொன்னதல்லால் வேறொன்றில்லை turns on what is to perish: 'said so that sin might cease' (scripture as a useful lie) or 'said only to destroy' (scripture as harm). On either, dharma and adharma, rebirth and the guru-disciple relation are placed among the things made up for a living (சீவனத்துக்கு). This is the run's conclusion and the Siddhars' most radical form of the attack on ritual religion; the reader is told to see (தெளிந்து காணே), not to believe.

links.note: Tirumular states what happens at death: the subtle body, having eaten what is in heaven and hell, goes on as the cause with its old deeds and takes a new body. Agasthiyar says no one has known where the life goes, and that 'joins the sky-Siva' and 'fire joins fire' are the sayings of those who do not know. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar's 'no one' includes the yogic account and not only the popular sayings he lists.

Sivavakkiyar says the Vedas, Agamas, treatises of truth and the teaching tied on (கட்டிவைத்த போதகம்), all the madness fit for stories, ended in nothing once he knew the Lord; Agasthiyar says the ancients tied on (மாட்டினார்) stories, kavyas and Puranas to bewilder. The same verb for scripture as something bound on from outside, and the same verdict.

Tirumular says the Lord set by grace, for souls, hell and heaven and endless births, no different from the earth; Agasthiyar says the Vedas and shastras made dharma and adharma, rebirth and noble birth, and that all of it is for livelihood. On a plain reading Agasthiyar denies what Tirumular affirms. The conflict softens only if Agasthiyar attacks the use made of these doctrines and not their truth, which the verse does not say.

The Kural says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not coming back, taking rebirth as real and release from it as the goal; Agasthiyar lists 'there is birth' among the things scripture made up for a living. The conflict depends on reading 2425 as denying rebirth rather than as mocking its preachers.

source_issues: 2422 has seven lines where the stanza form has eight, and lacks the antadi opening (தயங்க-) that 2421's close calls for; its first line is probably lost. The heading தயங்காமற் பிழைப்பதற்கே இந்த ஞானம் placed before it may itself be a displaced line.
2422 line 4 இயலான ரசந்தனிலீப் புகுந்தாற் போலும் is obscure and may be corrupt.
